- **Time Coefficients ($\mathbf{f}(t)$):** A vector of shape $\mathbb{R}^{R_t}$ containing the values of the basis functions at time $t$.
**Define Basis Functions:** Construct the vector $\mathbf{f}(t)$ using a set of sine and cosine functions, similar to positional encoding in neural radiance fields.
**Compute Features (Naive Approach):** For a spatial location $(x,y,z)$, retrieve the feature matrix $\mathbf{M}_{xyz} \in \mathbb{R}^{F \times R_t}$ from $\hat{\mathbf{V}}$.
**Memory Optimization (Tensor Decomposition):** Due to the memory cost of the naive approach, tensor decomposition is applied to factorize the volume into smaller components.
Multiply $\mathbf{f}(t)$ with the transposed decomposition matrices and vectors along the last dimension ($R_t$) to obtain time-specific matrices $\mathbf{M}$ and vectors $\mathbf{v}$.
Apply a weighted L1 loss to regularize the time-decomposed components $M_{Tr}$ and $v_{Tr}$.

- **Time Complexity:** Extremely high due to memory I/O bottlenecks in the naive implementation.
